prompt: What is the core difference between memoization and tabulation?
choices: Memoization is top-down (recursion plus a cache of results already computed); tabulation is bottom-up (an iteratively-filled table, no recursion)

prompt: The naive recursive Fibonacci function runs in exponential time because its recursion tree has O(2^n) calls. After memoizing it by caching on `n`, what is its time complexity, and why?
choices: O(n^2), because memoization still explores both recursive branches of every call before checking the cache
O(n), because there are only n+1 unique subproblems (fib(0) through fib(n)), and each is computed exactly once
O(2^n) still, because memoization only reduces memory use, not the number of computations
O(log n), because caching turns the recursion into an implicit binary search over n
